scheme_name: Microcredit Finance Scheme- Self Help Groups (DAADC)
description:
The Microcredit Finance Scheme for Self Help Groups (DAADC) is an initiative launched by the Government of India to empower women and promote self-reliance through microfinance. 

This scheme was introduced in 1999 under the Ministry of Rural Development. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to Self Help Groups (SHGs) to enable them to engage in income-generating activities. 

The scheme aims to empower women by promoting savings and providing access to credit. 

The target is to cover at least 1.5 million women through SHGs by the year 2025. 

The scheme also aims to enhance the socio-economic status of women by enabling them to become financially independent. 

Under this scheme, each SHG can avail of a loan amount ranging from INR 1 lakh to INR 10 lakh. 

The interest rate on these loans is typically around 7 to 10 percent per annum. 

The repayment period for the loans can extend up to 5 years. 

The scheme also encourages SHGs to engage in various livelihood activities such as agriculture, handicrafts, and small-scale industries. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily focused on women. 

Women aged 18 years and above can form or join SHGs. 

The annual income limit for the members of SHGs is set at INR 1.5 lakh. 

The SHGs must consist of a minimum of 10 members and a maximum of 20 members. 

All members must be from the same locality to ensure community bonding. 

The application process for the Microcredit Finance Scheme involves several steps. 

First, interested women must form a Self Help Group. 

The group must then register with the local government or the concerned department. 

The required documents for registration include identity proof, address proof, and a resolution signed by all members of the SHG. 

Once registered, the SHG can apply for a loan through a designated bank or financial institution. 

The application must include a project report detailing the intended use of the loan. 

The bank will then assess the application and may conduct a field visit to verify the details. 

If approved, the loan amount will be disbursed to the SHG’s bank account. 

The frequency of loan disbursement can vary based on the project and the financial institution’s policies. 

Typically, loans are disbursed within 15 to 30 days after approval. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Rural Development. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation through their respective departments. 

The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) is a key agency that supports the SHGs under this scheme. 

The NRLM provides training and capacity-building programs for SHG members. 

These programs aim to enhance their skills in managing finances and conducting business activities. 

The scheme has seen significant success since its inception. 

As of 2023, over 8 million SHGs have been formed across India. 

These SHGs have collectively benefited more than 100 million women. 

The cumulative savings of these SHGs have crossed INR 50,000 crore. 

The scheme has also contributed to poverty alleviation in rural areas. 

Studies indicate that households involved in SHGs have seen an increase in income by approximately 30 percent. 

The scheme has also led to improved access to education and healthcare for families of SHG members. 

The government has allocated INR 1,000 crore for the Microcredit Finance Scheme in the 2023-2024 budget. 

This funding is aimed at expanding the reach of SHGs and enhancing their financial capabilities. 

The scheme also promotes digital financial literacy among SHG members. 

Training sessions on digital transactions and financial management are conducted regularly. 

The SHGs are encouraged to open bank accounts to facilitate easy transactions. 

The government has partnered with various NGOs and financial institutions to provide additional support to SHGs. 

These partnerships aim to provide mentorship and market linkages for SHG products. 

The scheme also includes provisions for insurance coverage for SHG members. 

This insurance is aimed at providing financial security in case of unforeseen circumstances. 

The Microcredit Finance Scheme has been instrumental in promoting entrepreneurship among women. 

Many SHGs have successfully started small businesses and have become self-sustaining. 

The government continuously monitors the progress of the scheme through various evaluation mechanisms. 

Feedback from SHG members is also taken into account for improving the scheme. 

The success stories of SHGs are often showcased to inspire other women to join. 

The scheme has been recognized internationally for its impact on women's empowerment. 

It serves as a model for similar initiatives in other countries. 

In conclusion, the Microcredit Finance Scheme for Self Help Groups (DAADC) is a comprehensive initiative aimed at empowering women through financial inclusion. 

With specific targets and measurable outcomes, the scheme has made significant strides in improving the socio-economic status of women in India. 

The detailed application process and support from various government agencies ensure that eligible women can access the benefits of this scheme effectively. 

The ongoing commitment from the government to fund and support this initiative reflects its importance in the broader context of rural development and women's empowerment in India.
